rv.q: The performer’s verbal flexibility and perfect pacing make Man To Man compelling theatre.
Tilda Swinton has still got it.
Though all the choices here feel calculated to drag this play into 2026, it still doesn't quite make sense now.
But Karge’s overextended portrait of a woman who could be a modern Mother Courage becomes a test of endurance.
Really brave, engaging and emotive performance from Tilda Swinton.

Reuniting with director Stephen Unwin to reprise her role in Manfred Karge’s solo play at the Royal Court, the Hollywood star is a mesmerising stage presence, effortlessly shifting between the play’s female and male personas.

cn.t: Swinton mesmerizes in her long-awaited stage return, though critics are divided on Karge's fractured monologue. Her chameleonic performance and perfect pacing earn widespread praise, but some find the unconventional structure willfully obscure.
